problems: principality-of-vladimir-suzdal and ryazan are the later Cliopatria rows of states whose earlier rows (principality-of-rostov-suzdal 1056-1240, principality-of-ryazan 1094-1240) are in other batches' hands; those dossiers already name mine as successors, so I kept two dossiers per state to avoid two dossiers claiming the same shapes. If the orchestrator wants one dossier per state, move the keyframes into the earlier slug and run the end to 1389 (Vladimir-Suzdal) or 1521 (Ryazan); Cliopatria lacks 1241-1293 and 1241-1452 respectively.

principality-of-vladimir-suzdal ends 19 May 1389 (page: disestablished 1389; also 'since 1394' for the title); the Cliopatria shapes of 1395-1486 are marked wrong because they draw the Rostov/Yaroslavl/Uglich appanages. The Golden Horde dossier has vassal_start 1294 and vassal_end 1480 for this slug and needs re-aiming.

Cliopatria's Moscow shape already contains all of Tver from 1482 (annexed 12 September 1485) and all of Ryazan from 1521; the Ryazan and Tver dossiers' last years overlap Moscow's. Cliopatria's Moscow area (317,907 km2 in 1453-1462) is eight times the 39,000 km2 the Ivan III page gives for the end of Vasily II's reign.

Cliopatria draws Vladimir, capital of the Grand Principality, inside the Golden Horde / Blue Horde shape 1294-1400 and inside Moscow's from about 1420; the Vladimir-Suzdal shapes to 1389 are adjusted with a 70 km disc (same as the Rostov-Suzdal dossier).
Cliopatria's Tver is a quarter of the infobox area (7,100 against 28,450 km2): all Tver shapes adjusted.

Quotations come through WebFetch's extraction, not the raw pages; a claim the extraction added from my own prompt (Andrey Bolshoy 'of Uglich') was not used as page evidence. 'Principality of Rostov' is a redirect to the Vladimir-Suzdal article. The Tver page contradicts itself on the last Vladimir patent (1371 versus 1375); both are quoted. The Ryazan and Vasili III pages disagree on Ivan V's fate; both are quoted.
